Aroerite
a-RO-er-ite
n. (proper name; a man of Aroer, in the roll of David's mighty men)
Hebrew 'Aro'eri, the gentilic of Aroer. The place-name is connected with a word for a shrub of the desert, and three different Aroers are named in Scripture; which of them is meant here is not stated.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

The Aroerite appears once, at the close of David's roll of mighty men: “Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jehiel the sons of Hothan the Aroerite” (1 Chronicles 11:44). Hothan is named only as a father, and his two sons only as his sons, and all three only by the town they came from. This is the ordinary way of that chapter. The thirty are listed again and again by their villages — the Tekoite, the Antothite, the Baharumite, the Shaalbonite — and the effect of reading the list straight through is of a muster roll read aloud. These were not a caste. They came from scattered towns on both sides of Jordan, some of them from places Israel barely held, and they came to Hebron with one purpose: “All these men of war, that could keep rank, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel” (1 Chronicles 12:38). The Aroerite's sons are in the list because they came. Scripture keeps the names of men whose whole recorded act was to stand with the LORD's anointed when he had not yet been crowned, and that is honour enough to be written in a book that will outlast every throne.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Aroerite is a Hebrew gentilic and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Aroerite is a Hebrew proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears once, in 1 Chronicles 11:44.

It denotes a man of Aroer; Hothan the Aroerite was father of Shama and Jehiel.

Three distinct places named Aroer appear in Scripture.

The men are listed among David's mighty men, at the end of the roll.

Key Scripture

1Ch 11:44 — "Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jehiel the sons of Hothan the Aroerite,"

1Ch 12:38 — "All these men of war, that could keep rank, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king."

1Ch 11:10 — "These also are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who strengthened themselves with him in his kingdom, and with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel."

Heb 11:34 — "Quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens."

Modern Corruption

Lists of fighting men are read as royal propaganda; Chronicles presents them as men who came before there was a throne to profit by.

expand to see more

Rolls of a king's warriors are conventionally treated as court literature composed to flatter a dynasty. The detail of this list cuts against the reading. The men are identified by obscure villages, several of them outside Judah, many of them never mentioned again, and the chapter frames their coming as a strengthening of David in his kingdom before the kingdom was his in fact.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God records the service of the unknown. Hothan the Aroerite is a name, a town, and two sons. He is in Scripture because he stood where he ought to have stood. The Lord who promised that a cup of cold water would not lose its reward keeps books of exactly this kind.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Aro'eri, the gentilic of Aroer; Hothan the Aroerite, father of two of David's mighty men.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Aro'eri, a gentilic formed from the place-name Aroer.

Aroer is connected with a word for a desert shrub.

Scripture names three distinct places called Aroer.

Hothan the Aroerite is named only as the father of Shama and Jehiel.

The single occurrence closes the roll of David's mighty men.

Usage

"the sons of Hothan the Aroerite"

"came with a perfect heart to Hebron"

"who strengthened themselves with him in his kingdom"
